method: one long-lived `hdc shell` over a PTY, sentinel-terminated round trips; the transport floor is measured in the same session
question: TASK-IDC-001 concluded that a device-side resident injector (uitest start-daemon) was the path to the 400 ms p95 gate. This run tests that conclusion.

shell_builtin_echo.note: transport floor of the persistent channel

param_get.note: a trivial native OHOS binary: process start with no framework

uitest_help_only.note: uitest startup with no injection at all

findings: The resident daemon does not help. `uitest start-daemon` runs and stays resident (verified: pid parented to init), but uiInput latency with it (p50 334 / p95 424) is indistinguishable from without it (p50 326 / p95 413). The CLI is not a client of that daemon.

The cost is process startup, not injection. `uitest help`, which injects nothing, already costs p50 301 ms; the injection itself is therefore only ~34 ms. TASK-IDC-001's assumed remedy addressed a service connection that was never the bottleneck.
`uinput -T` is the faster closed surface: p95 332.9 ms, under the 400 ms gate, against uitest's 413.1 ms over it. Its own startup is 174 ms, so its injection costs ~100 ms.

uinput injection is real. A `uinput -T -m` swipe on the lock screen unlocked the device (this device has no passcode), so the events traverse the system input pipeline rather than being reported as accepted.

The two surfaces differ in what they refuse. uitest fail-closes on an off-panel coordinate (`Please confirm that the coordinate values are correct.`). uinput does not: it returns rc=0 with the hedge `If the command does not work as expected, check whether the specified coordinates exceed the screen boundary`, and only malformed arguments fail (rc=255).

uinput exposes a wider surface than the closed set needs (mouse, keyboard, touchpad, multi-finger, text) - a reason to keep lowering to an explicitly enumerated subset rather than passing anything through.
consequences: The gate is reachable inside the existing command surface, but only through uinput and only over a persistent channel; neither surface can meet it if a gesture pays a fresh Job's admission.
Choosing uinput moves the host-side frame bounds check from defence-in-depth to load-bearing: with uinput there is no device-side coordinate validation behind it.

Both surfaces remain startup-dominated. A genuinely low-latency path needs a resident process that keeps an injector loaded and accepts gestures over a channel; that is a device-side helper to be built, not a command to be called, and it stays out of the current scope.
device_state: the uitest daemon started for the comparison was killed; no uitest/uinput process remains; /data/local/tmp holds no probe files; the screen was returned to the off/locked state it was found in
